subject: On-prem gatekeeper + SAML/SCIM integration for private control plane
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@acmeretail.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Romero <claire.romero@acmeretail.com>
Date: 2028-08-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Integration kickoff: on-prem control plane + IdP mapping

Hi Irene,

Thanks for agreeing to run through our onboarding questions. We are planning a private deployment of Redwood's control plane inside our VPC (on-prem equivalent) and want to align on identity and access integration before the pilot. High-level asks:

- We need SAML SSO for user login against our Okta tenant (persistent NameID + groups).
- SCIM provisioning: create/update deprovision users & group sync; we need group -> RBAC mapping to Kubectl-like roles in the control plane.
- Service accounts: how do we map service principals (machine identities) to Redwood IAM roles? Can we do federated trust from our AD FS for long-running jobs?
- Audit+retention: what events are emitted to our SIEM and can we include SAML attributes in logs for traceability?

Attached I've included our current attribute map (acme-idp-attribute-map.csv) and a short list of questions the security team requires mapped to a runbook. Would appreciate a quick run-through of options and any recommended constraints (rate limits, retry/backoff, SCIM auth choices).

Next steps for us: pilot next week (2028-08-23) — would like to freeze integration decisions by Friday (2028-08-18).

Cheers,
Samir
Senior Cloud Engineer
Acme Retail Labs
[attachment: acme-idp-attribute-map.csv (CSV)]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-16T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Integration kickoff: on-prem control plane + IdP mapping

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear list and the attribute map. Good constraints on timeline; we can hit an integration decision by Friday with a short design and an implementation plan for your pilot week. Quick summary of our recommended approach, high-level: 

1) SAML SSO (Okta): persistent NameID (transient/persistent toggles) + groups in the assertion. We'll require the following attributes: email, displayName, groups (as multi-valued), and an immutable employee_id or user_id to correlate across provisioning and logs. See attached proposal (redwood-gatekeeper-proposal-v1.pdf) for specifics.

2) SCIM provisioning: Redwood will run a dedicated SCIM connector inside the customer's VPC that authenticates with a scoped SCIM token backed by a short-lived cert. This avoids egress to the public internet and lets you firewall by IP. SCIM will be configured for incremental provisioning (PUT for user create/update, PATCH for group membership deltas). We'll publish recommended rate limits; please see scim-rate-limits.xlsx.

3) Service accounts & federated machine identity: we support two patterns: (A) OIDC token exchange for short-lived service tokens (recommended for ephemeral jobs), and (B) long-lived service principals via a trusted IAM role mapping (for legacy batch workflows). For AD FS we can accept SAML assertions for initial mapping but will recommend switching to an OIDC flow for renewal.

4) RBAC mapping: we propose a gatekeeper component (redwood-priv-gatekeeper) that consumes SCIM group -> role mappings and enforces least-privilege roles (admin, operator, reader, billing). The gatekeeper stores bindings in the private control plane and emits audit events with the user_id and assertion attributes.

Action items I'm proposing:
- Internal: review gatekeeper role names and constraints (Markus, Evelyn)
- Implementation: kick Dev Patel for connector deployment pattern and helm charts

If that outline looks fine I'll produce a short technical runbook by end of day.

Best,
Irene
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-gatekeeper-proposal-v1.pdf (PDF)]

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@acmeretail.com>
Date: 2028-08-16T13:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Integration kickoff: on-prem control plane + IdP mapping

Irene — thanks, good doc. A few notes from the infra/security lens: 

- Gatekeeper role model: let's add a scoped "support:read-only" role (for our CS team access during triage) with breakglass approval flow. Avoid global "admin" unless truly needed.
- SCIM connector auth: prefer mTLS with mutual certs instead of bearer token if Acme can manage cert rotation; otherwise scoped API keys with IP allowlisting is acceptable.
- SCIM rate limits: confirm windowing strategy — we should recommend exponential backoff on 429 and Jitter to avoid thundering herd when re-syncing large groups.
- K8s/RBAC mapping: if the control plane exposes k8s-style RBAC, we should include a default mapping for group names with a regex prefix rule. I'll annotate redwood-gatekeeper-proposal-v1.pdf with concrete role -> resource mappings.

Markus
Head of Infra
Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@acmeretail.com>
Date: 2028-08-17T08:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Integration kickoff: on-prem control plane + IdP mapping

Couple of compliance items from my side: 

- Audit enrichment: include the SAML assertion ID and the persistent user_id in every audit event. Acme's SOC requires a linkage across identity provider logs and our control plane events.
- Retention: recommend configurable retention per tenant; default 90d full fidelity, 365d metadata only. Note this when you share the runbook with Acme.
- SCIM provisioning attest: we need a signed provisioning report after the first full sync that lists created/updated/deprovisioned accounts. We'll generate a templated report if Acme signs off.

Evelyn
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Integration kickoff: on-prem control plane + IdP mapping — Implementation tasks

Forwarding the thread to kick off the workstream. Samir, copied here are our implementation owners. Dev — please pick up these tasks and estimate. Priority: freeze decisions by COB today (2028-08-18).

Dev action items (initial):
- Helm chart for SCIM connector to run in Acme VPC (mTLS option + IP allowlist env var).
- Implement gatekeeper service skeleton that consumes a simple SCIM mapping JSON (group -> role).
- Audit event enrichment: include fields user_id, saml_assertion_id, source_idp_alias.
- Provide a short checklist for Acme for Okta config (NameID, group claim formatting, clock skew expectations).

Attachments: annotated proposal from Markus (see link in drive). Please include estimated dev hours and an ETA for a PoC (we are targeting pilot 2028-08-23).

Thanks — Irene

Irene / Dev / team — quick update from our side after a dry-run with Okta:

- Okta can deliver groups as a multi-valued claim and we can send immutable 'employeeNumber' as the persistent ID.
- We prefer mTLS for SCIM connector; our security team will manage cert rotation via our internal PKI.
- For service accounts we'll adopt OIDC token exchange for new workloads and map legacy AD FS principals via a one-time SAML assertion to create the service account.

We are good to proceed with your proposed approach. Dev, please send over the PoC helm chart and a minimal gatekeeper image we can run in our staging VPC. Also please include the provisioning attest template for our SOC audit.

Thanks,
Samir
